ops.text: Flake templates new projects start from (the root flake's `templates`: `nix flake init -t ~/vg-dotfiles#<name>`), each a dev shell, a .envrc for direnv and a starter program whose test is the flake's check; and Nix examples to learn from (dev-utils/nix-examples). Not part of any machine.

check.name: templates
check.notes: Per template, in a throwaway git repo: nix flake init, lock, `nix flake check -L` passes, the dev shell has its tool, the built program prints Hello, world!; control: with its test's expected greeting changed, the check fails and its log shows that expectation. Also a step of nix/scripts/check.sh. On Linux or macOS drop the `wsl -d NixOS --`.

ops.text: Every template starts a project whose own `nix flake check` passes, checked by starting one
ops.why: A template that only evaluates can still hand out a project that doesn't build (a missing Cargo.lock, a uv workspace with no uv.lock: the Python template was exactly that, a flake.nix alone). templates.test.sh inits each into a fresh git repo and runs its check, its program and its dev shell, and breaks each language template's test to show the check catches it. Verified 2026-11-01 on vgwsl2: all five pass, all four controls fail on their test's assertion.

ops.text: Templates follow nixos-26.05 and the toolbox: crane for Rust, bun for TypeScript, uv with uv2nix for Python, CMake and Ninja for C/C++
ops.why: The user asked to finish the language templates (2026-11-01) without naming languages; these are the ones the user's projects build with (toolbox: crane approved, bun instead of npm/yarn/pnpm, uv; C++ with CMake in oriens-cam), and nixpkgs follows the release branch (baseline rule nix.nixpkgs-release; crane needs 26.05). Each starts with no third-party dependencies (Python's only is pytest, from uv.lock) so its check runs in the sandbox; the Bun template says how to add a locked node_modules once it has dependencies.

ops.text: The default template: an empty dev shell (and a debug one on top) with places for packages and checks, loaded by direnv. Moved from the examples so it's a template like the others.

The Python template: a uv project (pyproject.toml, uv.lock, src layout) built with uv2nix, its virtualenv as the package, pytest against the installed package as the flake check, and a dev shell with the project installed editable.

ops.name: rust
ops.intent: The Rust template: built with crane (dependencies once, then the package, clippy with warnings denied, rustfmt and cargo test as flake checks over the same artifacts), and a dev shell with the same toolchain plus rust-analyzer.

ops.name: cpp
ops.intent: The C/C++ template: CMake and Ninja, a library the program and its CTest tests share, the build with its tests as the flake check, compile_commands.json for clangd, and a dev shell with clang-tools and a debugger.

ops.name: bun
ops.intent: The TypeScript template on Bun: bun test as the flake check, the program packaged as bun running its sources, and a dev shell with bun and the TypeScript language server.
